name: Ishmaiah
overview: Ishmaiah was a male chief officer for the tribe of Zebulun, serving in a leadership capacity as noted in 1 Chronicles 27:19. He is specifically identified as the son of Obadiah. Beyond his role and tribal affiliation, there are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Ishmaiah means 'YHWH heard,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's attentiveness. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 27:19 and is not indicated as being directly given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Ishmaiah was the son of Obadiah, as stated in 1 Chronicles 27:19. No other family relationships are documented beyond this father-son connection.
scriptureSignificance: Ishmaiah's significance lies primarily in his leadership role within the tribe of Zebulun as a chief officer, highlighting the organized tribal structure under King David's reign. His mention underscores the importance of faithful administration among the tribes of Israel. As the son of Obadiah, his lineage is briefly preserved, contributing to the genealogical and administrative record of Israel.
